record.title: Round three of the tool library: booking finished, repairs started
record.summary: An invented report for a test. The goal is met and five volunteers proved it. What they could not do, and what is still wrong, is listed.

data.for: the person who asked for round three

blocks.text:
# Round three of the tool library, reviewed

**This report is invented for a test.** Nothing in it happened, and every name, number and path in it
is made up. It stands in for a long report somebody really wrote, with the same shapes in it.

Written on 3 March 2031.

---

blocks.heading: The goal, in your words, and where it stands
blocks.text:
> *"A member can find a tool, book it for a weekend and see who has it now, without asking at the
> counter."*

**Met.** Five volunteers who had never used the library's screens booked a ladder, a drill and a
wallpaper steamer, start to finish, in about twelve minutes each.

> *"A volunteer can check many returns, note what is broken, and send one repair list at the end."*

**Met, and the "send one list" half is a count rather than a claim.** `GET /api/repairs` was read
four times during one check-in session and answered `0` every time. Then *Send the list*, and `1`.

**But two of the five could not finish without help**, and one of them lost six minutes on a single
step. Those failures are fixed and listed below; nobody has tried the fixes yet.

---

blocks.heading: What you asked for, and where each landed
blocks.text:
### Part A — finding a tool

| You asked | State |
|---|---|
| **1 · One count of tools everywhere** | **Done.** `src/shelf/count.ts` is the only place a shelf is counted, and the two pages now print **41 tools, 3 out and 2 broken** on both |
| **2 · Name, Shelf, Keeper, Note** | **Done.** *Where it lives* is gone — the shelf became a column you can change. A first-time member set all four in under a minute |
| **3 · The shelf editable after booking** | **Done, and it was worse than you thought.** It lost the note and said it had kept it. A note set aside now comes back when the shelf changes back |
| **4 · Search by what the tool does** | **Done.** "cut a pipe" finds the pipe cutter & the hacksaw, and says which words matched |
| **5 · Pictures of each tool** | **Done.** One picture per tool, taken at the counter, drawn beside its name and never stretched |
| **6 · Say who has it now** | **Done, with a date.** The row names the borrower's first name and the day it is due back, and *overdue* in words when it is late |
| **7 · Tools that come as a set** | **Done.** A set is one row with its parts under it; booking the set books every part, and a missing part is named |

### Part B — booking

| You asked | State |
|---|---|
| **8 · The weekend is a board** | **Done.** Book, move, stretch across Sunday, and say so when a booking runs past the weekend |
| **9 · One press to return a tool** | **Done.** Where a tool can come back in two states, the press opens both words rather than choosing |
| **10 · A note for the next borrower** | **Built, and it was behind a press nobody found.** See *What they could not do* |
| **11 · Bookings that clash** | **Done.** Two bookings of one tool on one day are refused at the door, and the refusal names the other booking and its day |
| **12 · Late returns in words** | **Done.** *Two days late* replaces `-2`, and a tool with no due day says *no day was set* rather than *0 days* |
| **13 · A waiting list** | **Done.** The next member on the list is told when the tool comes back, and nobody is told twice |
| **14 · Bookings in plain words** | **Done, without a model.** "next Saturday", "this weekend" and "the 14th to the 16th" are read by rules, and the board shows what it made of them |

### Parts C and D — repairs

| You asked | State |
|---|---|
| **15 · A repair is not a return** | **Done.** A repair is a row a volunteer claims; nothing starts one by itself |
| **16 · Right-click a tool to report it** | **Done** on a row, a booking and words selected inside a note. One small box, not three buttons |
| **17 · The repair list waits for Send** | **Done.** Notes are stored as they are written, so a reload cannot lose them |
| **18 · A repair says what it cost** | **Mostly.** Parts are counted in pounds and time in hours; a repair done for free says *nothing was spent* rather than showing a zero |
| **19 · Old repairs stay readable** | **Done.** A closed repair keeps its notes, its pictures and who closed it |

### Your addition — who fixes it

| You asked | State |
|---|---|
| **Suggest a volunteer from who fixed it last** | **Done.** Every suggestion carries the sentence saying why, and none is applied for you |
| **Do not guess; let me pick** | **Done.** One match is named with the words that matched; two or more are refused, naming each |
| **Say when nobody can fix it** | **Done.** With no volunteer who has fixed that kind of tool, the list says *nobody has fixed one yet* and offers everyone |
| **One repair may go to two volunteers** | **Done and counted.** One list, two volunteers, **two repairs**, and the reply says so in words |

---

blocks.heading: What was measured, not asserted
blocks.text:
**Nothing was sent before Send.** `0` repair lists, four times, then `1`.

**Each note kept the words it was about.** The stored list holds all three, each with the quote and
where it was — *the line "blade is loose" of the note on the jigsaw*. The deleted note is absent.

**The refusal is the same at both ends.** Book a tool that is out for repair: the board says
*"This tool is being mended and cannot be booked"* and greys the press; the booking door, reached
another way, answers **409** with the same sentence. Bookings before and after: **7 and 7.**

---

blocks.heading: What they could not do, and what changed afterwards
blocks.text:
These are the failures the volunteers wrote down. Each is fixed unless it says otherwise.

| What happened to them | Now |
|---|---|
| **The shelf page said nothing was out** while the count beside it said three were | Two sentences, both true. *Nothing is out today* and *nothing is overdue* are different facts |
| **The board's own arrow keys worked exactly once** — every press moved the focus away | The board holds its last answer while it reads the weekend again. Three presses, the same button each time |
| **There was nowhere to leave a note on a booking** | **Add a note** at rest, in the note's own place |
| **The repair box was cut off at the right edge** at 1440: *"epair"*, *"end"* | Fixed |
| **Nothing said you could report selected words.** Both found it by right-clicking at random | A press appears when words are selected, and it names them |
| **A note on selected words lost the words** in the repair list | The quote is drawn |
| **The due date was drawn as `2031-03-08T00:00:00Z`** on the phone | It says *Saturday 8 March* |
| **The search box cleared itself after every letter** on the phone | It keeps what was typed, and the list under it changes as you type |
| **A booking moved to the next weekend vanished with no hint of where it went** | It says which weekend it is on now, and takes you there |
| **Three things on screen were called Done** | The one that means the tool is back keeps the word; the other two say *stop editing* and *close this box* |
| **"null days", "1 field changed: data.shelf." and "a overdue"** | All three fixed. The first two were the stored words reaching a reader |

---

blocks.heading: What is still wrong
blocks.text:
**A booking made on paper cannot be moved on the board.** It now says so rather than doing nothing,
but the commonest thing you will want after reading it is to move it.

**Two volunteers on one weekend still overwrite each other.** The page no longer claims a state it
has not checked; the conflict underneath is untouched.

**The home page and the shelf page disagree about how many tools are overdue** — 2 against 4, with
near-identical labels. It was there before this round, a volunteer found it, and nothing changed it.

**A set with a missing part can still be booked.** The part is named on the row, but the booking
door does not refuse, so a member can arrive for a set that is not whole.

---

blocks.heading: What only you can decide
blocks.text:
- **Whether returning a tool should close its repair.** The last pass took a position and wrote
  down what the other choice would cost.
- **Whether a paper booking should get a row of its own**, so it can be moved.

---

blocks.heading: What this round deliberately did not build
blocks.text:
A loan page for members. Fines. A second library. Text messages. A model reading a date. Sign-in
from home. Any change to how a tool is priced.

---

blocks.heading: What proved it
blocks.text:
**61 test files, 1,204 tests, `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` all clean.**

**Every fix carries the change that proves its test can fail.** About forty of them: the count
reversed, the guard removed, the refusal deleted, the sentence put back. Two changes *failed to
fail*, and each was worth more than the fix it was testing —

- one proved a test could not tell a moved booking from a kept one, and it was made stronger;
- one proved a focus rule could be deleted with nothing going red, so it was deleted. The browser
  keeps the focus through the move it was written for.

**Five volunteers drove it in a browser**, each on their own copy of the library, and each stopped
their copy and checked its port was free again.

**Two migrations were applied**, each after a backup that was read back, and every row count was
unchanged. Three junk rows a test had written — *drill 2*, *drill 22* and *ladder test* — were
deleted, and this sentence is here because deleting them quietly would have been the same fault.

---
